rows.title: The mobile platform of Synapsis — Rules of this project
rows.summary: target language; a project's Nuclear never changes between the dialects of the platform (root rules 3 and 4).
body: - **The platform is Nuclear only.** Where a document describes what a project writes it names no dialect and no
target language; a project's Nuclear never changes between the dialects of the platform (root rules 3 and 4).
- **The contract comes first.** A kind, a decorator or a plugin exists when `platform.toml` lists it; the loader
refuses a dialect that leaves the list. A new one is added here, then in every dialect.
- **Data, not code.** The platform adds kinds and decorators only as data; language rules come from the base. A
generic mechanism belongs in the compiler; nothing specific to this platform or to its toolkit ever does.
- **The runtime works on web**: no `dart:isolate` nor `dart:io` without a `kIsWeb` guard.
- **Never edit by hand**: `docs/07-reference/` and `docs/08-guides/` without their tools (they are checked and
embedded in binaries), the Synapsis blocks of the flutter reference (`--fix` writes them), `examples/expected/`
(`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`), any `build/` folder.
- A change of the public API of a runtime package regenerates its type definitions
([docs/06-runbooks/runtime-release.md](docs/06-runbooks/runtime-release.md)).
- English everywhere. A change the user can see updates its documents in the same change. A decision is a new ADR
in `docs/03-adr/`; pending work is `docs/01-product/roadmap.md` and nowhere else.

body: Apps for Android, iOS, desktop and web through one UI toolkit, written once in Nuclear by the user and the agent.
This project holds what is the same for every dialect of the platform: its contract (`platform.toml`: kinds,
decorators, plugins, layout), its runtime packages (`synapsis`, `synapsis_genkit`), its examples and
its checks. ADR key: `mobile`.
Its only dialect today is `flutter`. It lives in `nuclearlang/dialects/dart/frameworks/flutter/` and is documented
by the [`dart` dialect project](../../../nuclearlang/dialects/dart/AGENTS.md): how the code comes out is read there,
never here. What the three platforms share (what a contract is, what the loader checks) is
[`platforms/`](../AGENTS.md); the framework is [`nuclear-synapsis-framework/`](../../AGENTS.md); the rules of the
whole tree are the root [`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md).

`BigDoubleJson`; a JSON number or another text is a `FormatException`); a local table compares and sorts their text

- Environments (spec 021): `env("NAME", "default")` in a mobile app reads the values of the environment it was built
for, constants of the build (`nuclear build --env <name>`); a secret read by the app is N0311. The example
`clean-flutter-project` reads `API_URL`.
- The flutter dialect's example `dart_extension` has its first comment in English (it was in Spanish), its output regenerated.
- Fixed: an `Http` connection whose `baseUrl` has no final `/` (`https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com`, as `nuclear gen
--source rest:<url>` writes it) sent every request to a wrong host. Found by the onboarding app `todos_app`.
- `examples/onboarding/todos_app` and the guide `onboarding-mobile.md`: a todos app made only by the tools.
- `nuclear add|remove <package>` is `flutter add|remove` (ADR-lang-0008); adding a package no longer fails in an app
without the AI plugin.
- First public version.

rows.title: Synapsis mobile — Why
rows.summary: Why
body: - An app carries the same http, JSON, state, session, routes and tests; here it writes only its business logic.
- What the UI toolkit lacks comes from `synapsis`, a package a Flutter developer may also use by hand.
- Left out on purpose: classes that only pass data around, a database for millions of rows.

rows.title: Glossary
rows.summary: Glossary
body: | Component | A business unit in `components/<name>/` with its own config, data, domain and presentation. Closed: another component sees only what the architecture rules allow | `components/` |
| Facade | The `appcomponent` of a component: what the screens and the other components see of it, usually an alias per use case | `components/<c>/<c>_component.nuc` |
| Global component | The kind `component`, in `shared/components/`: anyone uses it and its `@on(Event)` methods always receive | `shared/components/` |
| Connection | What a config declares to reach the outside: `Http`, `WebSocket`, an AI provider. Named with `connectionName`; the one without a name is the default | `appConfig`, `config` |
| State model | The states of a screen: each field is one state; a boolean field is a state without data | `presentation/<screen>/state_models/` |
| State manager | The kind `statemanager`: the state of one screen; its `@state` methods emit a state of its state model | `presentation/<screen>/managers/` |
| View | A `stateless` or a `stateful`. Only views use the UI toolkit's context and navigate | `presentation/` |
| Screen | A view with `@screen(route, ...)` | `presentation/<screen>/`, `shared/screens/` |
| Guard | The kind `guard`: an own access check, `canActivate()`, sync or async | `shared/guards/` |

rows.title: Vision — Problem
rows.summary: Between its screens and its backend, an app carries a lot of code that is the same in every app: http calls with cache and retries, JSON mapping, state handling, the injector, session, access control, events, routes, forms, translations, a local database, tests.
body: Between its screens and its backend, an app carries a lot of code that is the same in every app: http calls with
cache and retries, JSON mapping, state handling, the injector, session, access control, events, routes, forms,
translations, a local database, tests. The mobile platform lets a project write **only its business logic**, in
Nuclear; constructors, overrides, registration in the injector, serialization, http calls, state handling and
imports are written by the transpiler, and what the UI toolkit lacks comes from the platform's runtime.
The golden rule of the whole tree applies first: performance, speed and readability of the syntax. The platform's
own rules are the normative text: [mobile.md §3](../07-reference/mobile.md).

rows.title: Vision — Users
rows.summary: tests, identical for every dialect of the platform.
body: - **The user and the agent**, who write an app in Nuclear: kinds, decorators, folders, `config.nuc`, plugins and
tests, identical for every dialect of the platform. The agent's short sheet is
[brief/mobile.md](../07-reference/brief/mobile.md).
- **The author of a dialect**, who implements the contract (`platform.toml`) for a language and a UI toolkit.
- **A Flutter developer**, who may use the `synapsis` package by hand in any Flutter app: it is an independent
package.

rows.title: Vision — What it does not do
rows.summary: data around: the layers exist in the generated code.
body: - It does not describe how the target code is written: that is the dialect's.
- A project's Nuclear names no dialect and no storage engine, and it has no interfaces nor classes that only pass
data around: the layers exist in the generated code.
- A second dialect does not exist yet: `react-native` and `kotlin-multiplatform` are planned, not built.
- The local database is for what a phone shows, not for millions of rows.
- Translations use no third-party library.
- A backend and a web app are the other platforms of the framework
([`backend`](../../../backend/AGENTS.md), [`web`](../../../web/AGENTS.md)); an app reads a backend written in
Nuclear through its contract (ADR-synapsis-0006).

rows.title: Vision — What it is
rows.summary: Apps for Android, iOS, desktop and web through one UI toolkit.
body: Apps for Android, iOS, desktop and web through one UI toolkit. Three parts (ADR-dart-0001):
1. the **contract and its dialects**: `platform.toml` here; `flutter`, the only dialect today, in the
[`dart` dialect project](../../../../../nuclearlang/dialects/dart/AGENTS.md). Kinds and decorators add
behaviour: a `repository` with `@get` is the http call, the mapping and the cache;
2. the **runtime**: the `synapsis` package, and `synapsis_genkit` for the `genkit` plugin;
3. the **CLI and the editor extensions**, each its own project
([`tools/cli/`](../../../../../tools/cli/AGENTS.md), [`extensions/`](../../../../../extensions/AGENTS.md)).

rows.title: The local database — In the runtime
rows.summary: Android, iOS, Linux, macOS and Windows; IndexedDB on web).
body: - `Local`: the registry and the storage. One box per table, the same engine on every platform (a file per box on
Android, iOS, Linux, macOS and Windows; IndexedDB on web). `LocalDatabase(encrypted)` comes from the configs'
`local`, per component (`configure` / `settings`, the table's `component`). The AES key is made at the first
encrypted box and kept in the secure storage. `memory` keeps the boxes in memory, unencrypted, for tests.
`store` / `recall` use a calls box that remembers which rows each call (name, url and query) answered.
- `LocalTable<T>`: CRUD and the query builder over JSON rows (the model's own JSON mapping, nested objects
intact); the box is `synapsis_<name>`. `putRow` stamps `created` / `updated` (ISO-8601 texts) and gives
`generated` keys.
- `LocalQuery<T>` and the operators as top-level functions.
- An exact field (`bigint`, `bigdouble`): the row keeps its JSON text; the table's `exact` names those fields and
`valueOf` reads them as a `Decimal`, so `where` (equality, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `between`, `oneOf`, `ne`) and
`orderBy` compare by value, as the backend's SQLite does (ADR-backend-0003). The dialect writes `exact:` in the
model's table.
- `NotFound`: a `RepositoryError`, like `HttpError`; `attempt` catches both.
- `Repository.send(local:)`, `recall`, `target`, `local<T>()`, `saveLocal`.

rows.title: The local database — What a project writes
rows.summary: What a project writes
body: | Words | Effect |
| `@primary` on a model's key field | the model has a local table |
| `@primary(generated = true)` | the table gives the key (the field is optional) |
| `@created`, `@updated` | stamps the table writes |
| `@entity("table")` | the table's name; default: the model's name in snake_case |

| `local: LocalDatabase = LocalDatabase(encrypted = false)` in `appConfig` or in a component's `config` | how the tables are kept, for the project or for the tables of that component's models; the default is encrypted |
| `@repository(saveLocal = true)` | every GET of the repository that answers a model with a table (or a list of them) keeps its answer, and gets a twin |
| `@get(local = true)` | the same for one method |

| `<method>AsLocal()` | the twin: same signature and return type; it answers the rows that call answered, as they are now, and never sends a request. Without a previous answer it is an `Err` for a `Result` method |

| `local<M>()` in a repository method with a body | the table of `M`: `find`, `findAll`, `save`, `saveAll`, `remove`, `clear`, and the queries `where`, `orderBy`, `limit`, `offset`, `getOne`, `getMany`, `paginate` → `Page<T>`, `count`, `exists`, `update`, `delete` |

rows.title: The local database — What a project writes
rows.summary: is "is null" and `ne(null)` "is not null".
body: - The operators of `where` are `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `ne`, `like`, `ilike`, `oneOf`, `between`; a plain `null`
is "is null" and `ne(null)` "is not null". There is no `isNull`.
- A repository may be 100 % local: no http method at all.
- A GET that answers a generic (`Page<Character>`) is not kept: it has no key.
- `@column` is not part of the platform: in a document store the JSON name (`@key`) is the column.
- The Nuclear never names the storage engine.
- The generated tests call each twin and check it answers without a request.

rows.title: The runtime packages — Events
rows.summary: `Events.publish / subscribe`.
body: `Events.publish / subscribe`. Delivery is **on demand**: the visible screen gets the event at once; a hidden one
gets the last of each type when it is shown again. A `component` with `@on` always receives. Widgets
`EventBuilder`, `EventListener`, `GlobalEvents<T>`; mixin `EventsOnDemand`.
A background isolate publishes to the main one (not on web: no `ReceivePort` nor `IsolateNameServer` under
`kIsWeb`). An `event` has `eventName` and `toJson` / `fromJson`, so from another engine (workmanager) it travels as
JSON text and `Events.decoder`, registered at startup, reads it back. The backend publishes an event with the
header `x-app-event` (`EventInterceptor`).

rows.summary: `Log.d / i / s / w / e` (and the long names).
body: `Log.d / i / s / w / e` (and the long names). One block per log: the breadcrumb `component › kind › Class.method`,
the time, the message, `data` as JSON, the error, the stack, and the `.nuc` file and line at the foot, which the
transpiler writes in the call (`at`). A thick frame and a level badge in the colors of Bootstrap's dark alerts;
code colors in the breadcrumb and the data; Synapsis's own logs in purple; only the error's line blinks. A pastel
color per component (`LogColor`, a stable hash; `logColor` in the component's `config`).
- Release: only warn and error. `token`, `password`, `authorization`, `secret` and `cookie` are masked.
- `Log.level`, `Log.colors`, `Log.console`, `Log.sink` (a `LogEntry`).
- Flutter exceptions: `Log.catchFlutterErrors(app:)`, called at startup: a double red frame, the stack in columns,
a repeated error shown once.
- The package logs by itself http (request, response, error), the failures of a splash's `onLoad` and the
translations.
- Not caught: async errors outside Flutter (there is no `PlatformDispatcher.onError`).
Why: [ADR-mobile-0005](../03-adr/0005-readable-logs-by-component.md).

rows.title: Conventions
rows.summary: The rules of the whole tree are the root `AGENTS.md` (English everywhere, quality first, no commits unless the user asks).
body: The rules of the whole tree are the root [`AGENTS.md`](../../../../../AGENTS.md) (English everywhere, quality
first, no commits unless the user asks). These are the ones of this project.

rows.title: Conventions — `platform.toml`
rows.summary: How a contract is changed (the contract first, then every dialect, the `docs.toml` entry, the reference) is the same for the three platforms: changing a contract.
body: How a contract is changed (the contract first, then every dialect, the `docs.toml` entry, the reference) is the
same for the three platforms: [changing a contract](../../../docs/02-architecture/contract.md). In this one:
- The arguments of the data decorators are the same as the backend platform's (`[decorators.args]`).
- A removed decorator gets its line in `[decorators.replaced]`, so a project that still writes it is told what
replaces it (`N0309`).
- A generator template (`tools/code_generator/platforms/mobile/generators.toml`) writes finished, compiling Nuclear, each declaration under a comment that says what it is
for; `merge = true` on a declaration a later run may complete.
- Every new diagnostic code is documented in the language's
[diagnostics.md](../../../../../nuclearlang/docs/07-reference/diagnostics.md).

rows.title: Conventions — The documents
rows.summary: project writes, no questions, no history, no "pending".
body: - `docs/07-reference/mobile.md` holds only final rules and only Nuclear: no dialect's name where it says what a
project writes, no questions, no history, no "pending". Doubts go to the user; decisions become ADRs.
- A change the user of the platform can see updates its documents in the same change: the reference, the guide,
the context documents of this folder, the `CHANGELOG.md`.
- One fact, one file: what is the dialect's is linked in the
[`dart` dialect project](../../../../../nuclearlang/dialects/dart/AGENTS.md), never copied here.

rows.title: Conventions — The platform
rows.summary: here, TOML and templates in each dialect.
body: - Language rules come from the base. The platform adds **kinds and decorators only as data**: `platform.toml`
here, TOML and templates in each dialect.
- A generic mechanism belongs in the compiler (projects, decorator arguments, architecture names, call sites);
nothing specific to this platform, to a dialect or to a UI toolkit ever does. A template capability that is
missing is asked for as a generic one.
- Kinds and features may differ between platforms, never between the dialects of this one.
- The standard library is Nuclear's: a target's library name in platform code, reference, docs or examples is a
bug.

rows.title: Conventions — The runtime packages
rows.summary: import is left over.
body: - **They work on web**: no `dart:isolate` nor `dart:io` without a `kIsWeb` guard.
- The `synapsis` package re-exports nothing of the libraries it uses: each name is imported from its own, so no
import is left over.
- It stays an independent package: usable by hand in any Flutter app, with its README, CHANGELOG and `example/`.
- An app-wide service is a `Global` (`register`, `init`, `dispose`).
- Nothing the dialect generates names what is behind a service (the storage engine of the local database): the
generated code calls the package's classes, so the engine can change in the package alone.
- The package logs its own work through `Log` (http, the splash's failures, translations).
- Lints: `flutter_lints`; `flutter analyze` reports nothing.
- A change of the public API updates [synapsis.md](../07-reference/synapsis.md) and regenerates the type
definitions in the same change ([runbook](../06-runbooks/runtime-release.md)).

rows.title: Security and performance rules — Access
rows.summary: Access is denied by default.
body: Access is denied by default. A screen declares its rule in `@screen(loggedIn, acl)` and a use case in `@requires`
and `@acl`; the checks are the runtime's ([runtime.md](../02-architecture/runtime.md)). Privacy between components
is checked by the transpiler, not at run time ([project.md](../02-architecture/project.md)).

rows.title: Security and performance rules
rows.summary: Synapsis must warn when code breaks one of these.
body: Synapsis must warn when code breaks one of these.
| Topic | Rule |
| Headers | name / value pairs: `headers = { "Accept": "application/json" }` |
| Retries | automatic only on idempotent methods; POST and PATCH only with an explicit `retry` |
| Cache | purged when the session ends |
| WebSocket | `wss://` in production (`ws://` travels unencrypted) |
| Tokens | only `SessionManager` stores them (secure storage); never in annotations or config |
| Logs | mask sensitive data; no debug nor info in release |
| Network | no constant polling: only on connectivity changes and on demand |
| Events | typed (the kind `event`), delivered on demand |

rows.title: Security and performance rules — Sensitive data
rows.summary: Sensitive data
body: | Data | How it is protected |
| The session (data, token, roles, permissions) | the secure storage; it ends after its timeout without activity; an expired token is never sent and a 401 ends the session |

| The local database | encrypted unless a config says otherwise: AES-256 with a key generated once and kept in the secure storage. On web the key lives in the browser's storage, weaker than a phone's keystore ([ADR-mobile-0006](../03-adr/0006-local-database.md)) |
| Logs | `token`, `password`, `authorization`, `secret` and `cookie` are masked; release writes only warn and error |
| The key of an AI provider | a key written in an app can be read by anyone who has the app: for production prefer `FirebaseAI` or a remote flow on a server ([guide](../08-guides/genkit.md)) |

rows.title: Testing — The tests of an app
rows.summary: (ADR-mobile-0004, kinds.md).
body: - A project writes its tests in Nuclear: the kinds `tests` and `integration`
([ADR-mobile-0004](../03-adr/0004-tests-in-nuclear.md), [kinds.md](../02-architecture/kinds.md)).
- The build generates the standard ones: the JSON of the models, the contracts of the repositories, the guards of
the routes, a smoke test of the screens, the twins of the local database. In the `flutter` dialect they are one
file, `test/synapsis_generated_test.dart`. A field with a converter gets the JSON the converter writes
(`const Conv().toJson(DateTime(2000))`), or its `sample()` when it has one; an enum field gets its first value.
- The helpers are the runtime's: `package:synapsis/testing.dart`
([synapsis.md §7](../07-reference/synapsis.md)) and `package:synapsis_genkit/testing.dart`
(`startFakeGenkit`). `SynapsisTest.start` runs an app without network or device: fake http answers, the session
and the local database in memory.

rows.summary: 1. In the package: `flutter pub get && flutter test && flutter analyze`.
